title: A patch applier writes into a bare repository, where a file path is a hook: the write namespace includes executable code
index_line: T-0090 · EXEC · diffpatch applies a patch twice → add/add collision → three-way checkout writes hooks/post-index-change → hook runs · go · corroborated
invariant_violated: The patch handler assumed a patch can only add or modify content: paths are data, and a throwaway clone is inert. But the clone is a bare repository, whose root is $GIT_DIR — so a path such as hooks/post-index-change is not content at all, it is a program Git will run the next time it writes the index.

mechanism.does: a user with repository write access (obtainable through default open registration) submits a crafted patch to the diffpatch API
the handler applies the patch inside a shared bare temporary clone using --cached
submitting the same patch twice creates an add/add collision, so Git takes its three-way fallback path instead of the simple apply
the fallback checks the indexed path out; in a bare clone that path can be hooks/post-index-change
Git invokes the hook while writing the index
repository-controlled content runs as the Gitea service account

source.http.body.value: the diffpatch API request body: patch content whose paths are attacker-chosen

sink.file.write.value: the checkout of an indexed path inside the shared bare clone — a write that lands in $GIT_DIR

sink.exec.shell.value: Git executing hooks/post-index-change while writing the index

encoding.path.value: the path hooks/<name> is a filename in one namespace and an executable hook in the bare-repository namespace

guard.none.value: no restriction that patched paths stay outside $GIT_DIR/hooks, and no isolation of the temporary clone

preconditions.expr: the Gitea instance is reachable and its version is below 1.27.1
an account can be created (default open registration) and can create a repository
the diffpatch handler exists and applies patches in a bare clone

success: a hook file appears in the shared bare clone's hooks directory
a command from the hook runs as the Gitea service account (callback or file written outside the repo)
failure_like: the second identical patch is rejected without triggering a three-way fallback
patched paths are rejected when they resolve inside $GIT_DIR/hooks
false_positive: a normal patch applying cleanly is not this bug — the collision plus checkout is required
a hook file inside a *non-bare* working tree is inert; the bare clone is what makes it executable

hazards: any service that applies user-supplied patches, diffs or archives inside a repository it also treats as code
bare repositories put hooks/ and config at the root, so 'a file in the repo' and 'a program' are the same namespace
shared temporary clones carry state between requests, which is what makes the double-apply collision reachable
non_transfers: patch application in a separate working tree with hooks disabled (core.hooksPath set away)
services that reject patches touching reserved paths

provenance.author: Gitea Security Team (GHSA-rcr6-4jqh-j84m)
provenance.corroborates: CVE-2026-60004: the diffpatch endpoint applies attacker patches in a shared bare temporary clone; submitting the same patch twice creates an add/add collision and Git's three-way fallback checks the indexed path out despite --cached; in a bare clone the root is $GIT_DIR so an executable entry named hooks/post-index-change becomes a live Git hook, executed while writing the index

provenance.author: 0xBlackash (independent PoC)
provenance.corroborates: independent reproduction and writeup: crafted patches abuse Git hook execution during patch application in the diffpatch endpoint, yielding command execution as the Gitea service account; notes default open registration lets an unauthenticated visitor obtain the required repository write access

provenance.author: MITRE / NIST NVD
provenance.corroborates: CVE-2026-60004 description (RCE via diffpatch API through Git hook installation)
